deep.reconstruction:
The page is mostly sketches under one heading: "PD [?] variétés à bord fibrées sur v. à b. à fibres it[?] —". In English: manifolds with boundary fibred over manifolds with boundary, with fibres … The last word is unclear. "itérées" (iterated) is plausible but uncertain.

The heading names the programme the surrounding pages carry out. The aim is to resolve a tame ("modéré") stratified space into a family of compact manifolds with boundary or corners V_i°, one per stratum. The boundary pieces ∂_j V_i° of each piece are fibred over lower-stratum pieces V_j°. These fibrations must be compatible on corners, which makes them iterated fibrations.

The sketches illustrate local models of regular (tubular) neighbourhoods:
- Dumbbells: two discs (neighbourhoods of point strata) joined by a band of parallel strands (the tube around a 1-dimensional stratum ending on the points). They match the 'dumbbell' neighbourhoods U'', V^0, V^0' on the previous page.
- V-shaped wedges with rays: conical or corner neighbourhoods of a point stratum with incoming edges.
- A disc crossed by horizontal lines: a point stratum with several branches passing through it.
- Faint pencil drawings: half-erased versions of the same pictures.

The previous page builds nested neighbourhoods U_0 ⊂ U_1 ⊂ … ⊂ U_n. It peels off U_n^0, its boundary ∂U_n^0 and the pieces ∂_k U_n^0, giving a step-by-step construction (steps 1°–6°).

The next page formalises this. It defines fibrations ∂_j V_i° → V_j°. It gives a boundary formula, ∂(∂_j V_i°) = ∪_k (∂_j V_i° | ∂_k V_j°) ∪ ∂^{(1)}∂_j V_i°. It then sets up the triangular commutative diagram of V_{ijk…p}° with fibre-product squares (marked ×) and dimension counts.

In modern terms this is the 'dévissage' of a tame stratified space into a system of manifolds with corners and compatible proper fibrations. That is Thom–Mather control data, rephrased as Melrose / Albin–Leichtnam–Mazzeo–Piazza 'iterated fibration structures' or 'manifolds with fibred corners', equivalently the Ayala–Francis–Tanaka 'unzipping'. It is the theme Grothendieck announced in Esquisse d'un programme §5–6: a dévissage theorem, with an equivalence between tame spaces and such combinatorial-differential data.

ideas.what: Resolving a stratified space into manifolds with boundary whose boundary components fibre over the pieces of lower strata, compatibly and iteratively ('variétés à bord fibrées sur v. à b.').
ideas.modern_name: Iterated fibration structure / manifold with fibred corners; resolution ('unzipping') of a Thom–Mather stratified space; control data
ideas.usually_credited_to: Thom (1969), Mather (1970) for control data; Verona (1984); Melrose and Albin–Leichtnam–Mazzeo–Piazza (2012) for iterated fibration structures; Ayala–Francis–Tanaka (2017) for unzipping of conically smooth spaces
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984), §5–6: the dévissage of tame spaces and the conjectured equivalence with systems of manifolds with boundary and fibrations (circulated, not proved)

ideas.what: Local pictures of regular neighbourhoods: dumbbells (point strata joined by a tube around an edge stratum), wedges and conical neighbourhoods at point strata.
ideas.modern_name: Regular / tubular neighbourhoods of strata; conical local structure

missed.claim: The heading, together with the next page's diagrams, is an explicit 1974 formulation of what analysts later called 'iterated fibration structures' or 'manifolds with fibred corners' (Melrose school, ALMP 2012). It also matches the homotopy theorists' unzipping (AFT). The modern literature does not trace this notion back to Grothendieck's tame-topology dévissage, beyond general citations of the Esquisse.

missed.why_it_might_matter_today: The note documents that Grothendieck's dévissage programme was already formulated in this precise combinatorial form in 1974, a decade before the Esquisse. That is useful for historical attribution. Grothendieck's stated goal, an equivalence between the category of tame spaces and the category of such systems, remains only partially realised: AFT give a related ∞-categorical statement, but not in o-minimal / tame generality.
